scientific_disclaimers.oracle_triage_nature: Arm D triage policy relies on end-of-session cumulative counters (files, pivots, commands). This serves as an Oracle Upper Bound (hindsight retrospective policy), NOT an online early triage gatekeeper.
scientific_disclaimers.uniform_yield_assumption: Yield is modeled identically across all tiers (Y_observed), assuming attacker interaction is unaffected by honeypot persona. Under this assumption, Arm A (Static T1) trivially yields highest Yield/Rs (595.7) because its cost is near-zero (Rs 3.98), ignoring that detected low-interaction shells truncate deep attacker engagements.
scientific_disclaimers.strawman_caution: Arm D achieves 29.58x higher yield-per-rupee than static full virtualization (Arm C, Rs 2564.68), but has 0.0459x the yield-per-rupee of static cheap shell (Arm A, Rs 3.98) under uniform yield.
scientific_disclaimers.cost_basis: Nominal resource parameters based on Rs 2000/mo VPS assumption; empirical KVM benchmarks await Spike S2.
